title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government’s reply to the Committee’s 2020 report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards outlines its commitment to strengthen AI governance, focusing on transparency, accountability and public trust. It sets out concrete measures—including new regulations, oversight mechanisms and industry guidelines—to ensure AI systems are developed and deployed safely, ethically, and in line with societal values.

title: EM on EU Regulation 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence
description: The government's summary of an EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending several Regulations and Directives.
summary: This government memo explains the EU’s 2024/1689 AI regulation, which establishes uniform rules for artificial‑intelligence use across the Union. It revises and amends existing laws and directives to ensure AI products meet safety, transparency, and accountability standards.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual explains how it will monitor and manage the use of artificial intelligence in qualifications. The document was released after a request from education, science and business ministers.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyrighted works are used to train and develop AI systems, assessing the legal and ethical implications of that practice. It offers guidance on balancing the rights of creators with the need for innovation, outlining risks and recommending policies to ensure responsible use of copyrighted material in AI development.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government says it takes the House of Lords report on AI seriously, pledging to strengthen regulation, boost research and investment, and improve oversight to keep the UK at the forefront of AI development while managing risks. It stresses that there is no room for complacency, urging swift action to protect citizens, support economic growth, and maintain ethical standards.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document sets out the scope, objectives, and responsibilities of the Committee tasked with reviewing how artificial intelligence aligns with public standards. It also includes frequently asked questions to clarify the Committee’s approach, processes, and expectations for stakeholders.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee on the governance of artificial intelligence. In this submission, it outlines its views and recommendations for how AI should be regulated and monitored.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy explores how AI technologies are influencing the rules and oversight for medical products, ensuring safety, efficacy, and compliance with new standards. It emphasizes applying the AI White Paper's principles to develop clear guidelines that help regulators adapt to evolving AI‑driven medical devices and treatments.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the Defence organisation the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI leader for its size. It outlines a vision to advance AI capabilities, streamline deployment, and set high standards for responsible use across all defence operations.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will work with the transport industry to harness AI’s benefits while carefully managing its risks. It outlines specific steps to develop safe, efficient, and innovative AI solutions across the sector.
